title: Rockstar Reveals Drone Threat Forced Privacy Films on GTA 6 Offices
description: IGN reports that Rockstar Games revealed extreme security measures, including privacy films on buildings to block drones, in an employment tribunal regarding 31 fired GTA 6 developers.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Rockstar Reveals Extreme Security Measures to Protect GTA 6 Development

As anticipation reaches a fever pitch across the gaming community, the lengths to which developers must go to protect their crown jewels are becoming increasingly extreme. According to a recent report by IGN Games, Rockstar Games has shed light on the intense physical security measures surrounding the development of *GTA 6*, revealing that the studio was forced to install privacy films on its buildings after drones were utilized to snap photos directly through office windows.

### The Battle Against Modern Espionage

The revelation came to light in Rockstar’s opening statement submitted to the employment tribunal determining the fate of 31 *GTA 6* developers who were dismissed last year. While the core of the tribunal centers on the employment dispute, the filings provided a rare, unfiltered look into the paranoid and high-stakes environment of AAA game development. 

*GTA 6* has been a primary target for leaks, data miners, and bad actors for years, leading to massive early footage breaches and continuous insider scrutiny. By confirming that drones were actively deployed to peer through office windows—prompting the emergency application of privacy films—Rockstar underscored just how vulnerable traditional office spaces can be in the modern era of commercial espionage and relentless hype.

### Editor's Take

It is astonishing to see how high-stakes game development has transformed into an intelligence-style operation. The fact that drone surveillance has become a genuine operational threat to a studio like Rockstar highlights the intense pressure surrounding *GTA 6* and why protecting intellectual property today requires physical fortifications just as much as digital cybersecurity.
